age_bands.label: Infancy and early childhood
age_bands.description: Rapid growth and maturation of organ systems, immune education and neural development. Changes in this band are developmental, not aging.

age_bands.label: Childhood
age_bands.description: Continued growth and skill acquisition, with thymic output already declining from its early-life peak even as overall capacity increases.

age_bands.label: Adolescence
age_bands.description: Puberty and the approach to peak bone mass, muscle mass and several physiological capacities.

age_bands.label: Early adulthood
age_bands.description: The period in which most physiological capacities reach or hold near their lifetime peak, commonly used as a reference state for comparison.

age_bands.label: Middle adulthood
age_bands.description: Gradual, largely subclinical change across many systems, with wide individual variation in onset and rate.

age_bands.label: Later adulthood
age_bands.description: Age-associated changes become more readily measurable across multiple systems, and divergence between individuals widens further.

age_bands.label: Older adulthood
age_bands.description: Functional reserve narrows across systems and the distinction between normal aging and disease becomes harder to draw.
age_bands.data_sparsity_note: Cohort sizes shrink and survivor effects grow, so population averages in this band describe an increasingly selected group.

age_bands.label: 90 and over
age_bands.description: The oldest band, where survivorship selection is strong and curated data is sparse.
age_bands.data_sparsity_note: Data above 90 is sparse and drawn from small, highly selected cohorts. Treat population statements in this band as weakly supported.
